title: Ministry of Manpower (MOM) Singapore Employment Pass and COMPASS Framework
source: Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Government of Singapore
content:
The Employment Pass (EP) is Singapore's primary work pass for foreign professionals, managers, executives, and specialists sponsored by an established Singapore-registered enterprise.

Candidates must earn a qualifying fixed monthly salary that increases progressively with age, and pass the Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS). COMPASS evaluates applications across four foundational criteria: salary relative to local PMET norms, candidate qualification, company diversity, and support for local employment, requiring a minimum of 40 points.

First-time EPs are typically granted for two years and renewals for up to three years. Holders earning above statutory thresholds can sponsor family members on Dependant's Passes (DP) or Long-Term Visit Passes (LTVP).

title: Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) and Government Technology Agency (GovTech) Singpass
content:
Singpass (Singapore Personal Access) is the trusted national digital identity for every Singapore resident, including Employment Pass, S Pass, and Dependant's Pass holders.

Issued upon foreign identification number (FIN) issuance by MOM or ICA, Singpass provides secure biometric two-factor authentication (2FA) via the Singpass mobile app for more than 2,000 digital services across government agencies (IRAS taxes, CPF, CPF Housing, ICA) and commercial institutions (DBS, OCBC, UOB banking, telecommunications, telco eSIMs).

Foreign residents must register their Singpass account and maintain updated residential address details within 14 days of moving to avoid penalties under the National Registration Act.

title: Land Transport Authority (LTA) MRT Transit Network and SimplyGo Digital Ticketing
publisher: Ministry of Transport, Government of Singapore
content:
The Land Transport Authority oversees Singapore's extensive Mass Rapid Transit (MRT), Light Rail Transit (LRT), and public bus networks operated primarily by SMRT and SBS Transit.

Transit payments operate under the SimplyGo platform, allowing commuters to tap contactless Mastercard, Visa, NETS bank cards, and mobile wallets (Apple Pay, Google Pay) directly at train gantries and bus readers without topping up.

Fares are calculated based on total distance travelled rather than mode, meaning transfers between different bus routes or between buses and MRT lines within a 45-minute window are consolidated into a single continuous journey fare.

title: Ministry of Health (MOH) Singapore Healthcare System and Insurance Provisions for Foreigners
content:
Singapore's healthcare delivery combines primary care polyclinics, private General Practitioner (GP) clinics, and tertiary public and private hospital clusters (SingHealth, National Healthcare Group, NUHS).

Subsidized healthcare tiers and national MediShield Life health insurance are reserved strictly for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents. Employment Pass and foreign work pass holders pay unsubsidized, non-resident rates at public hospitals and polyclinics.

Employers of S Pass holders are legally required to provide mandatory medical insurance covering at least SGD 60,000 annually. Employment Pass holders typically receive private corporate health insurance from their employers or purchase private international comprehensive health plans.

title: Housing & Development Board (HDB) and URA Residential Tenancy Regulations in Singapore
source: Housing & Development Board (HDB) / Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA)
content:
Residential accommodations in Singapore comprise private condominiums/landed properties and public Housing & Development Board (HDB) flats. The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) mandates a minimum rental period of three consecutive months for private residential properties.

Short-term rentals (such as Airbnb) under three months in private residences and under six months in HDB flats are illegal in Singapore. Tenancy agreements typically require one month's security deposit for a one-year lease and two months' deposit for a two-year lease.

Foreigners renting HDB flats must hold valid immigration passes (EP, S Pass, Student Pass) with at least six months' validity at the point of application, subject to the Non-Citizen Subletting Quota for the neighbourhood and block.
